overview: A 9-pitch, 800-foot Grade III-ish line up the steep south face of Salish Peak, a striking spire just northeast of Three Fingers, climbing ramps, corners and short steep crux sections at a sustained 5.9-ish grade with two harder 5.10 pitches.

face: Roan Wall — center of the big red slab
overview: A 10-pitch, roughly 1,000-foot Grade III route up the center of Roan Wall, a big red slab split by a prominent corner system, on very high-quality granite with patina edges, friction slab, and cracks higher up.

face: Roan Wall — the rightward slab right of the wall's central corner system
overview: A 10-pitch, roughly 1,400-foot Grade III route up the rightward slab of Roan Wall, offering stacked pitches of quality face climbing with friction cruxes, corner work, and a unique finishing pitch with an overlap crack and low-angle face climbing.

overview: A 6-pitch, 800-foot Grade III alpine rock route up the prominent rib above the Martha's Place bivy boulder, mixing bolted face climbing with thin cracks on quality granite.
